title: Codex Ultimus: Tidal
statement: I have come back to Tessera's codex three times, with light, with seedlings and with nothing. This time I came back from the other theme. The sixty-four vellum tiles are a flat now: the sea has been over them and gone, and it stood higher in some tiles than others, so the grid reads as a tide table of its own, grey where the water still lies and pale where the vellum has dried, the levels following the same fortnight the Low Tide cards follow. Along the line the water reached furthest it has left a wrack of kelp across the glyphs, with the bladders I always draw. Barnacles have settled on the seal. The codex was a letter; it is also a shore. Whoever comes next can read the tide off the tiles or the glyphs off the tide.
process: I kept Tessera's paper field, octavo creases, 8x8 matrix and carmine seal, and flooded the grid by giving each tile a water level from the same spring-and-neap cycle as the tide table, drawing standing water in the high tiles and dry glyph lines in the low ones, then laid a hand-drawn wrack line with bladders across the grid and barnacles on the seal.
